transcribed_question:
A. Identify the structure fixed blue
B. The wall of the right ventricle is thinner than the left wall. True or false
C. List the dilations of the primitive heart tube
main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the blue pin.
main_explanation: The blue pin indicates the left auricle (atrium) of the heart.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a dilation of the primitive heart tube?
supporting_question.explanation: The primitive heart tube consists of five dilations: the truncus arteriosus, bulbus cordis, primitive ventricle, primitive atrium, and sinus venosus.

true_false.statement: The wall of the right ventricle is thinner than the wall of the left ventricle.
true_false.explanation: The left ventricle has a thicker myocardium because it must generate higher pressure to pump blood into the systemic circulation, whereas the right ventricle pumps blood into the low-pressure pulmonary circulation.
